articles.title: Vishnu Manchu’s Kannappa Takes YouTube By Storm, Draws Overwhelming Response
articles.description: Dynamic Star Vishnu Manchu's Kannappa is proving that its journey is far from over. After making a solid impact in theatres and on OTT, the film has now taken YouTube by storm, drawing an overwhelming response from audiences and introducing the epic devotional drama to an even wider section of viewers. The film has been witnessing phenomenal viewership on YouTube, with social media flooded by praise for Vishnu Manchu's committed performance and stunning transformation into the legendary devotee. Viewers, in particular, have been applauding the emotionally charged climax, where his intense performance has emerged as one of the film's biggest talking points. Along with the acting, audiences are appreciating Vishnu Manchu's courage and vision in producing a mythological spectacle of this scale with strong devotional values, something rarely attempted in recent times. Another major strength of Kannappa continues to be its soulful soundtrack, with the songs striking an emotional chord and adding immense depth to the narrative. The film also boasts an impressive ensemble cast, with Prabhas delivering a memorable special appearance that remains one of the biggest highlights. The presence of legendary actors Dr Mohan Babu, Mohanlal, Sarathkumar, Akshay Kumar, Kajal Aggarwal, Brahmanandam and several others further elevates the cinematic experience. Produced by Dr. M. Mohan Babu under the banners of 24 Frames Factory & AVAA Entertainment and directed by Mukesh Kumar Singh, Kannappa stands as one of the most ambitious devotional epics made in Indian cinema. With its remarkable resurgence through YouTube and growing admiration from viewers across the country, Kannappa has once again entered the spotlight. Watch Kannappa Full Movie below

articles.title: Scientists have found a billion-year-old hidden magma system on Mars that supported life on the Red planet
articles.description: Scientists have uncovered evidence of a massive magma system beneath Mars' surface, challenging the long-held belief that such complex geological activity requires tectonic plates. NASA's InSight lander data revealed a distinct boundary deep within the Martian crust, suggesting a vast, ancient magma chamber that cooled and crystallized. This discovery hints that the ingredients for life might be more common on Mars than previously thought, prompting a re-evaluation of planetary habitability.
